surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: The Sabres pile it on the Rangers
paras: Rasmus Dahlin got the scoring started for the Sabres just 17 seconds into the game. Josh Norris and Zach Benson scored 33 seconds apart early in the second to extend the lead to 3-0. Vladislav Gavrikov got the Rangers on the board with 46 seconds left in the period. Jack Quinn stretched the lead to 4-1 midway through the third, his fourth straight game with a goal. Jiří Kulich made it 5-1 two and a half minutes later.

The chances were closer than the score. Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen made 29 saves for the Sabres, and Joonas Korpisalo allowed five goals on 30 shots. The Sabres improved to 11-10-4, sixth in the Atlantic, while the Rangers dropped to 13-10-1, slipping to fourth in the Metropolitan.

items.text: Sam Carrick played his first game against the Rangers since leaving.
Zach Benson has a point in five straight games.
Matt Rempe was in NHL.com’s projected lineup, but Taylor Raddysh played instead.
None of the preview’s three calls held.
